Critical morphhb issue: Hebrew words use SLASH (/) to separate prefixes from root (e.g. b/7225 for be-reshit, d/8064 for ha-shamayim). Each part has its own morph code (HR/Ncfsa = preposition prefix + noun). The number of morphology parts MUST match the number of word parts (slashes). This means WLC word_count per verse may differ from verse text word count because morphhb counts compound elements separately.

WLC morph codes confirmed as OSHM format: HR/Ncfsa, HVqp3ms, HNcmpa, HTd/Ncbsa. LXX morph codes use dotted format: N.DSF, V.AAI3S, RA.NSM. Neither matches RMAC format (V-AAI-3S, N-NSM). Both will fail in explainEnding and verbTenseEs.

The eliranwong LXX-Rahlfs-1935 integrates CATSS morphology which uses a DIFFERENT format from Robinson. CATSS uses TYPE+PARSE (e.g. N1 NSF, V1 AAI3S) while Robinson uses dash-separated POS-TVMPN (e.g. V-AAI-3S, N-NSM). The LXX data in bible.db likely uses either CATSS or Robinson format depending on which source was ingested.

title: WLC word display is RTL in .original CSS but words are L-R logical order
detail: The .verse-line.original has direction:rtl CSS. Hebrew words in D.morphology are stored in logical L-R reading order (word_pos=1 is rightmost/first Hebrew word). The renderMorph function joins with ' ' space. In an RTL container, logical word order is reversed visually, so Hebrew word order SHOULD display correctly. However, sub-word prefixes (e.g. 'בְּ/רֵאשִׁ֖ית' = preposition+noun) are stored as single tokens with slash-notation - this is morphhb convention and is correct. No bug here but worth documenting.
